feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — The org chart is a symbolic construct rendered in visual form, not a bounded material object.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — Entirely designed and maintained by human institutions.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not inspired by or modeled on natural systems.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Not an energized or mechanized system.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Represents structure symbolically but does not function structurally.
feedback.Observable: Included — Its purpose is visibility and clarity; it is meant to be examined and interpreted.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Appears on screens or paper, but medium is incidental.
feedback.Active: Excluded — It is not an actor or autonomous process.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Built for clarity and formal delineation of reporting structures.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Enables decisions, but does not emit output autonomously.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Encodes structure but does not process data.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Communicates changes but does not cause them.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Included — Digital org charts are explored, searched, expanded — explicitly interactive.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Referenced by HR and management systems but not itself a subsystem.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Requires maintenance and user interpretation.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Organizations can operate without them, though less transparently.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Graphically maps roles and reporting relationships.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Communicates power, affiliation, and job status.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Must obey structural logic (trees, branches, reporting rules).
feedback.Compositional: Included — Built of nested roles and departments that reflect modular internal logic.
feedback.Normative: Included — Expresses and enforces norms of control, responsibility, and leadership.
feedback.Meta: Included — It is a model of an institutional model.
feedback.Temporal: Excluded — Not inherently bound to time (though it changes over time).
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Predominantly created, managed, and accessed via digital platforms.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Represents relationships that exist only by social agreement.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Constructed and maintained by formal authority structures.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Positions on the chart define professional identity and recognition.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Bound by internal HR and governance policies.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Determines resourcing, salary, and job allocation — a map of financial flows.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Changes to the chart reflect power shifts and are often contested.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Used ceremonially in promotions, onboarding, and reorg rollouts.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Raises questions about equity, bias, invisibility, and transparency.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the corporate org chart as a symbolic, hierarchical, and politically loaded abstraction. It is intentionally designed, visually interactive, and institutionally regulated. It is critical to identity, visibility, and economic structure within organizations, and functions as both representation and instrument of internal power.
